title: Container Bookings: effect of the customer's no-show record on new booking requests
content:
## Policy clause
For the Container Bookings product line, no-show behaviour is aggregated across the customer's whole booking portfolio. A new booking request for a tier may be accepted only when the customer's no-show count over the trailing 90 days is below that tier's no-show threshold. When the count has reached the threshold of the requested tier, the request is declined for that tier and nothing is charged; the customer may still request any tier whose threshold the count has not reached, subject to the booking request admission rules. Cancellations, declined requests and carrier rolls never count as no-shows.

## How the count is taken
- **What is counted**: the no-show fees booked on all of the customer's bookings, including fees later waived as goodwill, because the behaviour occurred.
- **Window**: the trailing 90 calendar days ending on the current request date, the request date itself included, across all bookings of the customer.
- **Evidence**: the no-show fee entries on the charge accounts of the customer's bookings, as the system records them before the request is decided; the count is tied to the requesting customer, not to one booking.

## Decision table
| No-show count in the window, compared with the requested tier's threshold | Result for that tier |
|---|---|
| Below the threshold | This condition is met; the request continues under the admission rules. |
| Equal to the threshold | Declined for that tier; nothing is charged. |
| Above the threshold | Declined for that tier; nothing is charged. |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)
*Hypothetical threshold of 3, for illustration only:* a customer with 2 no-show fees in the window meets this condition; a customer with exactly 3 has reached the threshold and is declined for that tier.

*Hypothetical dates, for illustration only:* for a request dated 30 June, the window is the 90 calendar days from 2 April to 30 June. A no-show fee dated 30 June counts; one dated 1 April does not.

## Points of judgement
**A no-show fee on another booking was waived as goodwill. Does it still count?** Yes. Waived no-show fees are counted.

**The customer cancelled two bookings last month. Do they count?** No. Cancellations never count as no-shows, nor do declined requests or carrier rolls.

**Is the customer barred from every tier once one threshold is reached?** No. Only tiers whose threshold the count has reached are closed; any other tier may still be requested under its admission rules.
